title: Kevin Thomas Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Kevin Thomas review, checked 20 Nov 2026: $4.99 to $1,999.95 across three storefronts, and all three of their own records show him losing.
dek: A handicapper who says he has sold picks since 2007 and today lists the same daily plays on Tony's Picks, SportsCapping and Wizard Sports Picks, at prices from $4.99 to $30 for the same single pick. Each storefront grades him itself, and on 20 Nov 2026 all three showed him below break even: about 49.7%, 48.9% and 50.8% winners, with units or dollars down on each.

short_answer: Kevin Thomas is a real, active seller. His picks appear on three marketplaces at once: Tony's Picks, a site run by Tony Tellez that lists about 29 cappers; SportsCapping, a large handicapper network; and Wizard Sports Picks, a newer site run alongside a horse racing picks brand known as The Wizard. Saved pages show him selling on SportsCapping as far back as 2014. In that narrow sense he is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is a different matter, and here the evidence is unusually clear because each store publishes its own grading. Tony's Picks showed 1,373 wins, 1,391 losses and 46 pushes, with units below zero for his whole history, for 2026 and for 2025. SportsCapping showed 218 wins and 228 losses since he joined its current platform in August 2025, down $2,123 at $100 a pick. Wizard Sports Picks publishes all 1,235 of his graded picks since October 2025; we downloaded them and counted 618 wins, 598 losses and 19 pushes, down 119.9 units, with the last 30 days at 41 and 52.

His sales copy points to winning slices: a strong June 2026, college football "since 2023", and WNBA. Some of those slices are real on the sellers' own logs; the totals are not winning. The same Friday pick sold for $30 on two sites and $4.99 on the third. We found no independent buyer posts about him, good or bad.

guarantee: The guarantee depends on where you buy. On Tony's Picks only his $30 single game packages are flagged as guaranteed, at the same $30 price, and we found no page that explains what that guarantee gives. Ask before relying on it.

SportsCapping's Profit Guarantee page says a guaranteed purchase that finishes with "a total profit of zero or less" ("breaking even counts") earns the next day of picks free, a guaranteed subscription "is automatically extended by its original length," some accounts get account credit instead, "Season and rest-of-season passes are not guaranteed," and "Guarantees apply once per purchase."

Wizard Sports Picks says in its FAQ: "If the pick doesn’t turn a profit you’ll automatically receive a full credit equal to your purchase price," and "Only your initial purchase carries a guarantee." That is site credit, not cash.

Tony's Picks terms deal with auto renewing memberships: a buyer must email "within 3 days of your next automatic renewal date" to stop it and get a refund or credit for that period, and a 3 day trial must be cancelled 48 hours before it renews. None of the three stores covers losses on the bets themselves, which are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: Wizard Sports Picks shows every graded pick it has for him, 1,235 rows from 2 Oct 2025 to 19 Nov 2026, each with the price and the stake in units. We downloaded the full table on 20 Nov 2026 and totaled wins, losses and units by season, sport and month ourselves. For SportsCapping we added up the per sport lines its profile publishes. For Tony's Picks we read the win, loss and unit totals in its store data. Each figure is graded by the store that sells him, not by an outside auditor.

The pattern is the same everywhere: his sales copy is built from real slices that look good (a 63% June, a 60% college football season in 2025, 58% in the WNBA), while the full logs on the same sites sit near or below 50% and lose money. On Wizard his months since October 2025 were winners only in October to December 2025, March 2026 and June 2026, and the last two months were his worst: October 2026 at 43-52-1 (-53.9 units) and November so far at 23-32-1 (-52.9 units).

The "55% since 2023" college football figure cannot be checked before 2025, since none of the stores shows his picks from 2023 and 2024. Where the stores do overlap with that window, the result is mixed: winning on Wizard in 2025, losing on Wizard in 2026 and losing on SportsCapping overall.
The unit figures on Tony's Picks use a scale the site does not explain (a 50-28-1 month showed as +2246 units), so we compare its win and loss counts rather than its units.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: no third party audit. We found no outside tracker, contest record, court case or regulator action about him.

Tony's Picks: on 20 Nov 2026 its store data listed 1,373 wins, 1,391 losses and 46 pushes (49.7% of decided picks), units of minus 8,945 lifetime, minus 2,968 for 2026 and minus 2,512 for 2025. Over the last 30 days he was at minus 1,180, 26th of the 29 cappers on the site; the last 7 days were up 213. On 16 Nov the same data read 1,366 and 1,388.

SportsCapping: his current profile says member since August 2025 with 453 picks. Adding its per sport lines gives 218 wins and 228 losses, down $2,123 at $100 a pick: college football 55-66 (-$1,777), MLB 51-56 (-$42), WNBA 47-32 (+$1,239), NFL 39-39 (-$383), NBA 6-12 (-$725), NFL preseason 7-10 (-$412), NHL 7-7 (+$47), college basketball 6-6 (-$70). The page counts 2 winning months out of 7 and 10 winning weeks out of 23, and labels August 2026 his most profitable month at 37-35. His free picks there were 28-20 since 31 Aug 2025.

Wizard Sports Picks: all 1,235 graded picks since 2 Oct 2025 total 618-598-19 (50.8%) and minus 119.9 units at the site's stakes, which average about 1.9 units to risk per pick. By year: 2025 (October to December) 148-123-7, up 13.1 units; 2026 so far 470-475-12, down 133.0 units. By sport: WNBA 84-62 (+18.0), NHL 41-42-3 (+3.1), college football 93-78-7 (-19.0), MLB 114-126-2 (-18.3), college basketball 93-104-4 (-24.4), NBA 115-108-3 (-37.3), NFL 78-78 (-42.0).

Older history: SportsCapping pages saved in May 2014 and July 2017 show Kevin Thomas selling day, 3 day, 7 day and 30 day passes and season passes there, with a bio saying he had been capping "for well over 12 years" and had a circle of trainers and physical therapists. The 2014 page promised a free next day if a day pass did not profit; by 2017 the 30 day pass promised money back in site credit. The records from those years are not shown on the current platform.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Kevin Thomas pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Kevin Thomas performs beyond what the selling sites publish.
our_data.context: For scale: the three selling sites show him at about 48.9% to 50.8% winners overall, while the 30 day run Tony's Picks promoted in July 2026 was about 64%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found no independent buyer reviews of Kevin Thomas. Below is what we searched, what little exists, and the reviews of the marketplace that sells him.

customers.text: We found no post from anyone who says they bought Kevin Thomas picks, good or bad. We searched Covers, Sportsbook Review and TheRX through the web, our saved copies of ten betting subreddits and the newest r/sportsbetting and r/sportsbook posts, CapperTek, the Better Business Bureau and general review searches. The few Reddit posts that matched his name were unrelated golf pool and daily odds threads. What exists is seller side: Tony's Picks blog posts praising one strong month in June 2026, his free pick articles, a 2026 video interview on the Wizard Sports Picks channel, and reposts of his plays by pick sharing accounts on X, which say nothing about how buyers fared. The only buyer reviews we found are four CapperTek reviews of the Tony's Picks marketplace from 2019 to 2024, all negative, none naming him. With no buyer posts there is no smoke to report about him personally; the strongest evidence on this page is the sellers' own records.

The Tony's Picks blog ranked him first over the past 30 days at 49-31-1 and said he was nearly 800 units ahead of second place. The post was written by the marketplace owner, so it is not independent evidence.
A follow up post again put him at the top of the 30 day board, at 50-28-1 for +2246 units. Same author, same marketplace.

A Wizard Sports Picks video interview presents him as a professional with over twenty years in the business and walks through his NFL, college football and WNBA percentages. Three of the four percentages match the site's own log; the current NFL figure did not.

CapperTek lists four reviews of TonysPicks.com, all negative. Reviewers describe losing records after paying, including one who said they were down about $6,000 on a $599 monthly plan in February 2024, and one who complained about heavy favorites. None of the four names Kevin Thomas, so they describe the marketplace, not his picks.
The Better Business Bureau lists Tony's Picks in Ontario, California, business started 22 May 2005, not accredited and not rated, with no complaints filed in the last 3 years.
No Reddit, Covers, Sportsbook Review or TheRX thread about Kevin Thomas the handicapper turned up in our searches, and we found no review page, regulator action or court record naming him.

conflicts: Every record and ranking we saw comes from a store that earns money when his packages sell. The Tony's Picks blog posts and the Wizard video are marketing.
The stores' own logs contradict their marketing: a top month in June 2026 and a strong 2025 college football season, but losing totals on all three sites.
His background differs by store: math teaching on Tony's Picks, physical therapy studies on SportsCapping and Wizard.
The same pick sells for $30 on two stores and $4.99 on the third, so the price you pay depends on where you happen to land.
strengths: Prices for every package are listed on all three stores.
Wizard Sports Picks publishes every graded pick with the line, price and stake, so a buyer can check his record before paying, as we did.
He writes free pick articles with his reasoning, and his free picks on SportsCapping were 28-20 since August 2025.
Some slices are genuinely positive on the sellers' own logs: WNBA (84-62 on Wizard, 47-32 on SportsCapping) and the 2025 college football season (53-35-4).
A long history: saved pages show him selling on SportsCapping since at least 2014.
concerns: All three stores' own records show him below break even overall, and the last two months on Wizard were his worst.
Sales copy highlights chosen slices and contains at least one figure (60% NFL this season) that the store's own log did not match.
His Navy and college background is told two different ways.
Guarantees differ by store, pay in credit or free picks, and the Tony's Picks guarantee is not explained anywhere we could find.
Prices for the same plays vary from $4.99 to $30, and the three day pass description on Tony's Picks still shows an old price.
No independent buyer reviews at all.
checklist: Before buying anywhere, open the Wizard Sports Picks history table or the SportsCapping profile and look at the full record, not the package headline.
Compare prices across the three stores; the same pick can cost six times more on one than another.
Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A 30 day leaderboard is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% month can sit inside a losing year.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension before you pay for it, and watch automatic renewals on Tony's Picks.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
faq: He is a real handicapper with active profiles, published prices and free pick articles on three marketplaces, and saved pages show him selling since at least 2014. We could not verify that his picks win over time; in fact all three stores' own records showed him below break even on 20 Nov 2026. We found no independent buyer reviews and no court or regulator action involving him.
On Tony's Picks (run by Tony Tellez), on the SportsCapping network and on Wizard Sports Picks. The same daily plays appeared on all three on 20 Nov 2026.
How much does Kevin Thomas cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 single picks were $30 on Tony's Picks and SportsCapping and $4.99 on Wizard Sports Picks. Three day passes ran $89.99 to $109, 30 days $329.99 to $429.99, a year $1,999.95 on SportsCapping, and NFL season passes $699.99 to $999.99.

Not in cash. SportsCapping gives free replacement time or account credit on guaranteed packages, Wizard gives site credit on guaranteed picks, and Tony's Picks only refunds or credits an auto renewal if you email in time. Season passes carry no guarantee anywhere.
Does Kevin Thomas have a verified record?
No independent one. The stores that sell him grade his picks: Tony's Picks shows 1,373-1,391-46, SportsCapping 218-228 since August 2025, and Wizard 618-598-19 since October 2025, all losing money.

He has had strong stretches, such as June 2026 and the WNBA, but the full records on the sites that sell him show losses for 2026 and overall. Nothing refunds your betting losses, so if you try him, buy the cheapest version of the shortest package and track every pick yourself.
